parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of CreateTaskUseCase does what an application-layer use case should. It checks the input, confirms that the referenced project and assignee exist through domain repository interfaces, builds the Task entity, saves it through TaskRepository and maps the result to a TaskOutput DTO. The problem is in execute(). Each failure path passes an HTTP status code (400 or 404) to ApplicationError, so the use case is deciding the HTTP response for each outcome. Turning application outcomes into HTTP status codes is a job for the transport layer, here infrastructure (e.g. TaskController / http-server). This ties the use case to HTTP. A smaller point: Task invariants such as "title and description are required" and the default status "todo" are enforced here rather than in the domain entity. I could not see Task, so I am not sure about that point, and the status-code coupling is the main reason for the fail.

violations.message: CreateTaskUseCase.execute() passes HTTP status codes (400, 404) to ApplicationError. Mapping outcomes to HTTP responses is a transport (infrastructure) job, not an application-layer one. The use case should raise transport-neutral errors (e.g. ValidationError, NotFoundError), and the infrastructure controller should map them to HTTP status codes.
